At the museum, you'll see demonstrations related to its location on the equator, including swirling water, balancing an egg and walking along the equator line.

The museum also introduces you to the Indigenous cultures of South America. Exhibits cover the tsantsa ritual, totems, traditional dwellings and everyday objects.

The main stops today are the Basilica del Voto Nacional, Plaza Grande, the Golden Church, Plaza San Francisco, El Panecillo, Intiñan and Mitad del Mundo.

Return to your hotel and spend the evening at leisure.

Accommodation is at the 4-star Finlandia. Breakfast is included.
A bust on a stone pedestal and an obelisk against a mountain backdrop near Quito, Ecuador

After breakfast, set out for Quilotoa crater lake. The first stop is a rose farm in the Cotopaxi Valley, where roses of different colours and sizes are grown for export. You'll see how the flowers are cut, sorted and packed. The rose farm visit is unavailable on weekends and public holidays.

Continue through the village of Tigua and visit a workshop known for its naïve painting style, in which Andean landscapes are traditionally painted on sheepskin. The group then follows the Pujilí Route to the village of Quilotoa, where a lookout offers views of the crater lake. The itinerary also includes a walk through an Indigenous community.

If the whole group wishes, you can walk down to the lake, go kayaking and ride mules back up. Kayaking and mule rides are extra. Local residents offer mule rides as an informal service, usually until about 3 pm.

The main stops are the rose farm, the viewpoints, the Indigenous art gallery and the crater lake.

After the excursion, transfer to Baños. Accommodation is at the 3-star La Floresta. Breakfast is included.
